facts.statement: The holotype specimen, consisting of a lower jaw fragment and twenty teeth, was discovered in the Dinosaur Beds of Malawi between 1987 and 1992.
facts.quote: The holotype (specimen Mal-175), consisting solely of part of a lower mandible and twenty isolated teeth, were found in the Dinosaur Beds of Malawi between 1987 and 1992.

facts.statement: Karongasaurus holds the distinction of being the first dinosaur named in a publication released entirely online.
facts.quote: Karongasaurus was the first dinosaur named in a publication that was published solely online

facts.statement: The type species Karongasaurus gittelmani was described by Elizabeth Gomani in 2005.
facts.quote: The type species, K. gittelmani, was described by Elizabeth Gomani in 2005.

facts.statement: The lower jaw of Karongasaurus is U-shaped when viewed from above, and its teeth are slender and conical.
facts.quote: The mandible of Karongasaurus is U-shaped in dorsal view and the teeth are described as slender and conical in shape

facts.statement: Karongasaurus was a small sauropod reaching 9 meters in length with a slender build and a weight of only 1 tonne.
facts.quote: Karongasaurus era un saurópodo de pequeño tamaño que alcanzó los 9 metros de largo y de delgada constitución con sólo 1 tonelada de peso.

facts.statement: The fossil record for Karongasaurus spans from 121.4 to 113.2 million years ago during the Aptian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Aptian to Aptian (121.4 to 113.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: Elizabeth Gomani classified Karongasaurus within the group Titanosauria in 2005.
Karongasaurus belongs to the infraorder Sauropoda.
Karongasaurus is assigned to the unranked family Titanosauria.
Remains of Karongasaurus were found in the Mwakasyunguti area within the Karonga District, north of Malawi.
facts.quote: Sus restos fueron encontrados en el área de Mwakasyunguti en el distrito de Karonga, al norte de Malaui

rejected.statement: Karongasaurus lived during the mid-Cretaceous, approximately 116 million years ago in the Aptian stage, in what is now Africa.
